## Predictive Stability and Adaptation Under Distribution Shift: Calibration, Discrimination, and Decision Thresholds in Credit-Risk Modeling {#distribution-shift}

<p class="authors">Silas Bambil and Shudeshna Nandy</p>

A model can still rank cases well while its predicted probabilities become unreliable. This study examines how changes in the deployment population affect calibration, discrimination, probability accuracy, and classification decisions.

::: {.finding}
**What the study shows**

The appropriate updating strategy depends on what changes. Intercept recalibration can address baseline-risk changes, while changes in predictor effects may require full refitting. Adjusting a decision threshold addresses classification decisions rather than probability calibration.
:::

<details class="methods"><summary>Study design & methods</summary>

The study combines a loan-default benchmark with controlled Monte Carlo experiments. Scenarios include covariate shift with model misspecification, baseline-risk changes, and changes in predictor effects.

Comparisons include retaining the original model, intercept-only recalibration, intercept-and-slope recalibration, importance-weighted refitting, and full deployment refitting. Threshold revision is evaluated separately, with independent data used for final performance assessment.

</details>

<div class="tags"><span>Logistic regression</span><span>Calibration</span><span>Monte Carlo</span><span>Credit risk</span></div>

## Stable Fire-Loss Quantiles and Far-Tail Expected Shortfall Gaps {#fire-loss}

<p class="authors">Silas Bambil</p>

An analysis of approximately 1.25 million positive-loss U.S. structure-fire records from NFIRS, covering 2016–2025. The study uses extreme value methods to examine catastrophic loss severity and uncertainty in the far tail.

::: {.finding}
**What the study shows**

Extreme-loss quantiles were comparatively stable across modeling choices. Expected Shortfall was more sensitive to threshold selection and uncertainty in the far tail, making the distinction between these risk measures consequential.
:::

<details class="methods"><summary>Data, modeling & robustness</summary>

Peaks-Over-Threshold methods and Generalized Pareto models are used to estimate Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall. Robustness checks include threshold sensitivity, parametric bootstrap, annual tail estimation, leave-one-year-out analysis, event-level aggregation, goodness-of-fit diagnostics, and competing tail models.

</details>

<div class="tags"><span>Extreme value theory</span><span>Tail risk</span><span>Bootstrap</span><span>NFIRS</span></div>

[Code & reproducibility materials](https://github.com/sdbambil1/nfirs-extreme-value-analysis){.button}
:::

## In development {#in-development}

<span class="badge planned">Planned follow-up study</span>

### Allocating Deployment Labels Between Model Updating and Intervention Selection Under Distribution Shift

How should a fixed labeling budget be divided between updating a model and selecting an updating intervention? Planned comparisons include all-label refitting, fixed fitting–validation splits, cross-fitting, and adaptive allocation, with final evaluation on untouched test data.
:::

<span class="badge planned">Planned computational project</span>

A project examining the numerical accuracy and computational efficiency of logistic recalibration methods under changing data distributions.
